statement: Tom gives away half of his marbles. Now he has 6 marbles left. How many marbles did he give away?

choices.misconception: I took half of the 6 marbles he has left.
I added half of 6 to the 6 he has left.
I found how many marbles he had at the start, not how many he gave away.
I added the 6 he has left to the 12 he started with.

hints: If he gave away half, what is the other half?
Halving makes two equal parts: the part he gave away and the part he kept. Think about how big those two parts are compared with each other.
The 6 marbles he kept are one half. The marbles he gave away are the other half.

solutions.reliable: Half means two equal parts. The marbles he kept and the marbles he gave away are the two halves, so they are the same size. He kept 6, so he gave away 6. Check: he started with 6 + 6 = 12, and half of 12 is 6. The idea to keep: the two halves of something are always equal, so knowing one half tells you the other.

whyOnTest: This checks that you understand halves as two equal parts, and the starting amount is the tempting wrong answer.
